title: Check yourself: What to keep, where it failed and what must not be logged

questions.stem: A platform handles two million conversations a day and cannot afford to store every trace. Users report wrong answers that the dashboards do not show. Which rule fits best?

options.text: Keep all failures, slow calls and complaints, and sample the rest by id
options.says: Tail-based sampling can look at the outcome, so it retains what failed, what was slow and what a user flagged, and takes a share of the rest by id.

options.text: Raise the random share from one percent to five, and review that larger share each week
options.says: Ruled out because "a random share of one percent holds almost none of them, and five percent holds few more".

options.text: Keep only the requests of the largest customers, because their heavy usage dominates
options.says: Ruled out because "Sampling by customer size covers heavy use and says nothing about which requests failed".

options.text: Store metrics only, and rely on the daily error count, since that costs almost nothing
options.says: Ruled out because a metric "says that something changed. It never says where or why".

origin.section: What to keep when you cannot keep everything

questions.stem: In one trace, the orchestrator, a researcher agent and a download tool all show an error. The orchestrator's message says the research step failed. Where does the failure originate?

options.text: In the orchestrator, because it is the first component the user's request reached
options.says: Ruled out because "the first span to turn red is not the origin".

options.text: In the researcher, because it is the first agent below the orchestrator to show an error
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "The span that reports an error is often only passing on the error of the span below it".

options.text: In the deepest span that broke, the call at the bottom of the chain
options.says: The deepest failing span is the origin, and the spans above it only relay its error.

options.text: In the planning model call, because a poor plan would send the researcher to a bad source
options.says: Ruled out because the fix is to "Read the trace to the deepest failure", and the deepest failure here is the tool, not a model call.
